description: The bar chart illustrates the annual distribution of hateful communication datasets from 2012 to 2022, categorized by the top five researcher locations (USA, UK, India, Italy, Germany) and a combined “Other” category, with the vertical axis representing the number of datasets on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10² (100). Each year along the horizontal axis features a grouped set of colored bars corresponding to researcher locations as defined in the legend: blue for “Other,” red for UK, orange for USA, purple for IT (Italy), green for IN (India), and brown for DE (Germany). The USA consistently leads in dataset production across most years, with its output peaking in 2020 at approximately 30 datasets and again in 2021 at around 40. India’s contribution shows marked growth, surpassing the UK in 2021 (with ~25 datasets vs. ~18 for the UK) and maintaining a higher output in 2022 (~8 vs. ~7). The UK’s output fluctuates but generally declines after 2019. Germany’s dataset production peaks in 2020 (~20) and then declines steadily through 2022 (~8). Italy’s output rises notably in 2019 (~8) and 2021 (~12) but drops sharply in 2022 (~1). The “Other” category shows substantial growth, particularly from 2017 onward, reaching its highest point in 2021 (~100 datasets) before declining slightly in 2022 (~30). The chart visually emphasizes the dominance of USA-based researchers and the rising contribution from India, while also highlighting the declining trend from Germany and the volatile but growing role of researchers from other locations.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of datasets over time for the five most frequent researcher locations and all other locations combined, spanning the years 2012 to 2022. The horizontal axis represents the years, while the vertical axis indicates the number of datasets on an exponential scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^2. Researchers from the USA consistently published the highest number of datasets across all years, with a peak in 2020. Notably, researchers from India surpassed those from the UK in dataset production in 2021, marking a significant shift in contributions. Additionally, the number of datasets from Germany declined steadily after 2018, indicating reduced activity in dataset production from this region.
